body: # Consumer Price Index Data from 1913 to 2026. The Consumer Price Index (CPI-U), published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) within the U.S. Department of Labor, is the primary measure used to track inflation in the United States. The latest CPI update was released June 10, covering inflation data through May 2026. The next CPI report is scheduled for July 14, 2026, and will include inflation figures through June 2026. **What Is the Consumer Price Index (CPI)?**. Before exploring the historical inflation data below, you may want to learn more about how the Consumer Price Index measures inflation. The first chart below illustrates price changes over time across major CPI categories, showing how inflation has affected different parts of the economy. The chart tracks percentage price changes from January 2019 through May 2026. Hover over the chart to view specific data points, or select a category from the legend on the right to highlight it. ### Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) from 1913 to 2026\*.

On this page are inflation rates and consumer-price-index data for the United States, from 1913 until 2023. For more recent data, please find the appropriate pages in the main menu. Data is extracted from the Bureau of Labor Statistics database and is updated monthly. Click on a year to see the monthly inflation rates for that specific year. ← Slide left and right to view more. | Year | Yearly CPI | Yearly Inflation Rate |. Sign up to receive CPI Inflation Calculator's monthly alerts, and you'll be the **first** to know when inflation changes. All CPI data was provided by the *Bureau of Labor Statistics* on **June 10, 2026** for the month of **May 2026**.
